payload.prompt: A realistic, continuous 5-second video of a young Asian woman writing and annotating text on a transparent glass writing board against a matte black background. She wears a plain black T-shirt and blue jeans and holds a bright neon-yellow marker in her right hand. The camera is fixed, medium-wide shot, straight-on perspective, professional studio lighting. The board is completely blank at the start. The glass is perfectly clear with no reflection of her, no mirrored double, no ghost image, and no second figure visible anywhere in or behind the glass -- only one woman is ever visible in the frame, at the center, and the area behind and beside the glass is plain matte black with nothing else in it. Ink only appears exactly underneath the moving marker tip, one stroke at a time, never ahead of the tip, never appearing all at once or partially formed before the tip draws it. Her handwriting is small and compact, staying on a single horizontal line without wrapping to a second line. She looks at the board, raises her hand, and writes exactly this text at the top-left of the board: "I vibe-coded my app" -- reproduced exactly, character for character, with no extra punctuation of any kind added anywhere. "$99" is written as a dollar sign followed directly by the two digits "9" and "9" with no period, space, or extra digit between them. "x.country" is written with a period between "x" and "country", never a hyphen or dash, and with a lowercase "x". After this clip's stroke is completely finished, she does not look at the camera. Keeping her eyes on the board, she lifts the marker tip slightly off the glass so it leaves no ink, and moves her hand steadily through the air to a blank position directly below this line, at its left edge, ready to begin the next line of text, her head slowly turning to follow her hand the whole way -- one continuous, slow motion, not a cut. By the final frame of this clip, her hand and the marker tip are at rest at that new position, ready for the next stroke, not still at the position where this clip's stroke ended. The camera holds steady the entire time.
